chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim from Hamdan ibn Ishaq who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — or it was narrated to me from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — the doubt is from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Tus, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.'

He said: So I performed Hajj after the visitation, and I met Ayyub ibn Nuh. He said to me: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of my father in Tus, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed, and He will build for him a pulpit beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and 'Ali (peace be upon him), until Allah finishes the reckoning of the creatures.'
So I saw Ayyub ibn Nuh after that, and he had visited, and he said: 'I have come seeking the pulpit!'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Rida in Tus according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the unique spiritual status of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) by promising complete forgiveness of sins and a permanent, elevated pulpit (minbar) beside the Prophet and Imam Ali (a.s.) in the Hereafter. The anecdote of Ayyub ibn Nuh seeking his 'pulpot' illustrates the tangible, almost physical nature of this reward in Shia eschatological imagination, emphasizing the intercessory and honorific role of the Imams. This narrative reinforces the concept of *tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, linking earthly devotion to eternal proximity to divine authority.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb both narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥamdān ibn Isḥāq, who said: I heard – or a man heard – Abā Ja’far (Imam Jawād (a.s.)) say, “Allāh forgives the past and future sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of my father (a.s.) in Ťūs.”

After performing the Ziyārah, I went for Hajj where I met Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ. He said to me, “Abū Ja’far (Imam Jawād (a.s.)) has said, ‘Allāh forgives the past and future sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of my father (a.s.) in Ťūs and (on the Day of Judgment) He will set up a pulpit for them beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and the pulpit of ‘Ali (a.s.) where they will sit until Allāh finishes judging the creation.”

Thereafter, I met with Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ again and he had come to the Ziyārah (of Imam Riďā (a.s.)) and he said, “I have come seeking the pulpit!” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain, and others, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ḥamdān ibn Isḥāq, from Abī Ja’far (a.s.) – or from someone from Abī Ja’far (a.s.).
